classification_signals: The paper is explicitly labeled 'REVIEW' on page 1.

It synthesizes existing literature on insect and mammalian navigation, but also presents original empirical findings from 'our laboratory' (p. 2, 7, 10) using methods like extracellular recordings, calcium imaging, and lesion studies, making it a narrative review with empirical contributions.
title: Spatial Navigation and the Central Complex: Sensory Acquisition, Orientation, and Motor Control

limitations: The question whether insect CX cells are 'real' head direction cells remains to be addressed (p. 9).
The specifics of the CX's role in controlling insect behavior will vary from insect to insect and behavior to behavior (p. 14).
The extent of the areas affected by electrical stimulation in the CX is not clear (p. 8).
minimum_safe_summary: This review paper synthesizes findings on the role of the insect Central Complex (CX) in spatial navigation, sensory acquisition, orientation, and motor control, drawing comparisons to mammalian navigation systems. The authors present empirical data from their laboratory showing that cockroach CX neurons integrate visual and mechanosensory cues, encode head direction and rotation history, and are involved in controlling walking speed and turning behaviors. Lesions and chemical ablation of the CX impair navigation and optomotor responses, while electrical stimulation can evoke speed changes and turns. CX activity often precedes movement, and its population code for locomotion is dynamic and context-dependent, suggesting a pivotal role in guiding insect behavior. Limitations include the need to further validate if insect CX cells are true head direction cells and understanding the variability of CX function across different insect species and behaviors.
